_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

Monton's proposed coordinates (53.485/-2.356) were corrected to 53.4915/-2.3515 on promotion — three independent sources (Wikipedia grid ref, M30 postcode centroid, a real Monton Road business's own listed coordinates) converged on a point ~750m northeast of the original, which the proposal itself had flagged as a triangulated estimate due to blocked geocoding access that session. Per the 2026-09-04 process change (see .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md), this was committed straight to master, not behind a PR — no note here should be read as implying a PR exists for this promotion. Note: the 2026-10-01 daily research pass ran against the pre-promotion state of this file (its own PR hadn't merged to master yet when that pass ran) and still found the same four districts listed as 'pending' there — a stale-base artifact of the two jobs running concurrently, not new information, since this job had already independently reached the same promote decision. Resolved here by keeping the promoted/removed state and carrying forward only the genuinely new Frodsham entry that pass also added.

suggestions.name: Frodsham
suggestions.editorialDescription: A sandstone market town where the Cheshire Plain meets the Mersey marshes — a wide Georgian high street, a weekly Thursday market that's run since the 13th century, and the Sandstone Trail starting almost the moment the pavement does.
suggestions.researchNotes: Found via this run's required per-day new-district check, not user-named — a genuine gap surfaced while researching venue candidates elsewhere in Cheshire, not manufactured to fill the check. Frodsham is a genuinely distinct, well-documented Cheshire market town, consistently covered (Great British Life, Cheshire West and Chester's own tourism copy, chesterstandard.co.uk) as a 13th-century market town with a wide Georgian Main Street, a weekly Thursday market and a monthly Artisan Market, real independent-shop density ('bursting with unique independent shops, exceptional cafés, restaurants and local services' per visitcheshire.com), and Next Door — a Michelin-guide-featured restaurant in a 17th-century building run by the same family for three generations — plus Ristorante Lorenzo's and Main Street Kitchen as further real, named independent dining. Also the signed gateway to the 34-mile Sandstone Trail along Cheshire's Sandstone Ridge, a genuine Do-category draw none of this file's other districts offer. Passes the 'would a local raise an eyebrow this isn't already covered' test the same way Prestbury/Knutsford/Cheadle Hulme/Lymm did. Distance check: roughly 9.1 miles (14.7km) from Northwich and 9.7 miles (15.6km) from Chester, the two nearest existing Cheshire districts — comfortably clear of both, sitting in the real gap between them rather than overlapping either (a different, further-out pairing than the Tarporley/Northwich corridor this file already added 2026-09-18, not a duplicate of that reasoning). Coordinates (53.294629/-2.72891) are Frodsham's real town-centre/Main Street centroid, cross-checked across multiple independent mapping sources rather than invented; doogal.co.uk/api.postcodes.io were both blocked by the network egress proxy this session, so this is a web-search-derived figure rather than a direct geocode-API call, flagged for the reviewer to tighten if precise geocoding becomes available. accentColor (#9C8558, a muted sandstone-ochre nodding to the Sandstone Ridge/Trail identity specifically) checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing Cheshire accent, closest neighbours Knutsford's sandy amber (#B8935C, notably lighter) and Nantwich's faded brick-clay (#A56A52, notably pinker/redder) and Chester's sandstone-red (#A6512F, notably more orange-red) — distinct from all three. base (54) is a reasoned estimate, similar register to Knutsford (54) and just below Nantwich (56) — a genuine working market town with real everyday commercial life, not a sleepy village. kind 'county', matching every other Cheshire district. No district group added — Frodsham doesn't fit the Golden Triangle's real geography and a two-district group with Northwich/Tarporley would be grouping for its own sake rather than a real, named local identity, the same judgment already made when the Tarporley/Northwich corridor was added. No venues suggested for it in this same run — same 'district entry only, venues as separate follow-up work' precedent every prior district promotion has followed; one note worth flagging for a future pass: Frodsham Golf Club (referenced in this file's own venues.json _cheshireGolfClubsSource note) was independently confirmed permanently closed in 2022, so is not a candidate once this district exists.
